question: Will Renan Santos win the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Lula leads the 2026 Brazilian presidential race in first-round polling at roughly 36-38%, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro at 29-34%, with Augusto Cury and smaller right-wing or centrist names trailing in single digits. Recent Quaest surveys show the two frontrunners tied near 41% in runoff simulations, narrowing from Lula’s earlier edge after turmoil at the Supreme Court energized conservative voters and lifted Flávio’s support. Jair Bolsonaro remains ineligible due to his legal status following the 2022 post-election events. The October 4 first round and potential October 25 runoff hinge on turnout among swing voters, coalition consolidation on the right, and any further shifts from institutional disputes or campaign messaging on security and the economy. Trader pricing reflects this competitive dynamic between the incumbent Workers’ Party candidate and the Liberal Party challenger.
